claim_scope: Research-only SHADOW evidence for one governed same-occurrence ZDEX buy-and-burn module transition. Python and Rust bind an exact governed V2 Spot purchase, combine prior buyback reserve with the current fee allocation, credit only the profile-selected canonical pool principal, burn exactly the received ZDEX, reject nonempty consumed-object tuples in the primary composer and GlobalSettlementABI V1 epoch verifier, and retain a nonzero lane-coordination obligation after the burn receipt. Rust derives and binds the complete tokenomics fee, cadence, and supply state. Its purchase and burn witnesses share one externally verified opaque authority statement covering profile, generation, policy registry, verifier registry, root image, and receipt-verifier binding. Python returns an opaque accepted result that binds the recomputed pending transition and exact burn receipt. Python also demonstrates exact global state/effect refinement for the composed occurrence. Lean proves the abstract transition is total, rejection is an exact no-op, accepted accounting conserves quote value and burns exact output, and lane coordination remains pending. ESSO proves a separate finite commit model only when all modeled lane, global-refinement, and current-authority premises hold.
